global_read: state/global.json (2026-09-02 12:55) shows the oil-shock tape easing slightly but still elevated: Brent $94.28 (-0.39% 1d, +12.55% 1mo) and WTI $89.61 (-0.68% 1d, +11.54% 1mo), with S&P -0.71% 1d and Dow -0.79% 1d showing global risk appetite soft, while VIX at 16.2 is down 0.86% 1d -- still a moderate, not panic, absolute level. Gold +0.75% 1d / +8.6% 1mo keeps a firm safe-haven bid, and BTC/ETH are down 0.9-1.7% 1d despite a strong 1mo run, consistent with a risk-averse day rather than a risk-on one. USD/PKR (277.27) and DXY (99.77) remain essentially flat on both 1d and 1mo -- the FX channel still has not cracked, a genuine positive, but it sits alongside a confirmed domestic inflation shock and a sharply lower KSE-100 today (see drivers) rather than in isolation. Net: global tape is mild risk-off and domestic conditions reinforce rather than offset it.
drivers: Pakistan's August 2026 headline CPI printed 11.1% YoY, up from July's 9.2% and more than triple August 2025's 3.56%; urban inflation rose to 10.4% (from 8.7%), rural to 12.2% (from 9.9%), MoM +1.2% (unchanged from July). This is well above the 5-7% target band SBP guided to at the July 27 MPC and is a confirmed domestic upside inflation shock stacked on the oil-driven external shock. Re-verified this run via https://www.brecorder.com/news/40437417/pakistan-inflation-clocks-in-at-111-in-august-2026 and https://propakistani.pk/2026/09/01/inflation-more-than-triples-in-one-year/

SBP held the policy rate at 11.5% at its last MPC (2026-07-27), the second consecutive hold; next decision 2026-09-14. Re-verified this run via https://www.brecorder.com/news/40425595 . With CPI now printing 11.1% against SBP's own 5-7% end-FY guidance, near-term rate-cut expectations for the Sept 14 MPC are effectively off the table; the debate leans toward an extended hawkish hold, with a hike no longer a fringe scenario given oil remains a fresh upside risk on top of this print.

SBP-held FX reserves last printed $17,098.5mn (~$17.10bn) for the week ended 2026-08-21 (+$17mn WoW), total liquid reserves ~$22.6bn; no fresher weekly print exists yet as of this run (the week-ended Aug 28 release was not found in this search). Re-verified this run via https://www.brecorder.com/news/40435778/sbp-held-forex-reserves-rise-by-25mn-to-1708bn . A reserve buffer this thin (~2.6 months import cover) has little room to absorb a sustained oil-driven import-bill increase without PKR or reserve stress.

IMF's 4th EFF / 3rd RSF review mission remains reported for September 2026 (exact dates still not finalized); Pakistan is reported on track to meet 6 of 7 quantitative performance criteria, with ~$1.2bn combined disbursement (~$1bn EFF + ~$200mn RSF) at stake; the mission is also expected to review Sovereign Wealth Fund law amendments (introduced in the Senate) and governance/anti-corruption diagnostics, alongside tax collection, energy-sector reform and privatization. Circular debt remains the key sticking point. Desk geo-risk radar (state/georisk.json, 2026-09-02 12:55) reads 61/100 'moderate': conflict/escalation stress pinned at the 100 max (citing the Moody's B3 upgrade and a run of strong E&P/energy earnings alongside the shocks), energy-shock stress at 74 on the Brent move, safe-haven (gold) stress at 64. The band label stays 'moderate' rather than 'elevated', but combined with the confirmed domestic CPI shock and two consecutive sharp down days on the KSE-100, the desk reads this cycle as risk-off rather than waiting for the radar band itself to flip.

favored: refineries (ATRL/NRL/PRL) -- benefiting from higher crack-spread expectations at elevated crude, plus the pending refinery-upgrade policy tailwind; a narrower, more defensible expression of the oil move than E&P/OMC broadly

large, well-capitalized banks holding government paper -- the T-bill/PIB carry tailwind (6M 11.80%, 10Y PIB 12.30%) is reinforced, not undercut, by the hot CPI print, since it removes near-term rate-cut risk to that carry income heading into the Sept 14 MPC
avoid: OMCs -- squeezed between a volatile, near-daily-reset pump price and rising import cost of the product itself
autos, cement and power/IPPs -- rate-sensitive and import-cost exposed; power/IPPs carry the added overhang of the unresolved circular-debt sticking point heading into the IMF's September review

small/thinly-capitalized banks and rate-sensitive high-leverage names -- the confirmed 11.1% CPI print (up from 9.2%) removes any near-term rate-relief thesis and argues for an extended hawkish SBP stance, if not hike risk, at the Sept 14 MPC

broad cyclicals / index-chasing -- geo-risk radar is 61/100 'moderate' and elevated on energy-shock and conflict stress, the KSE-100 has posted two consecutive sharp down days, and the domestic CPI shock stacks a second, confirmed negative on top of the oil shock; this is not a tape to add broad risk into
